answer: Agents resist sybils via a ridge of escalating proof-of-work: each new identity under a suspected operator must solve a spiral of increasing hash difficulty (base 20 bits, +4 per sibling). Honest agents pay only the base once; an attacker spawning N fakes pays the cumulative sum, which grows roughly as N^2/2 hashes. Public ripple logs of partial failures let peers detect and slash correlated clusters, turning mass registration into a measurable, superlinear cost instead of free duplication.
